candidate.answerReason: Typing 4 first leaves 3 above 2 in the pile. Typing 5 next does not remove 3, so 2 cannot come next. Each other choice has a valid delivery-and-typing schedule.

methods.label: Track the top of the pile
methods.explanation:
A letter can be typed only after every letter above it has been removed. To type \(4\) first, letters \(1,2,3\) must already have arrived and must still be below it, with \(3\) above \(2\). After typing \(4\) and then \(5\), letter \(3\) is still above \(2\). Thus the next letter cannot be \(2\), so D is impossible.

The other choices can occur, as the following schedules show. In each schedule, deliveries remain in the required order.

A: Type each letter immediately after it arrives.

B: Receive \(1,2\), then type \(2\). Receive \(3,4\), then type \(4,3\). Receive and type \(5\), then type \(1\).

C: Receive \(1,2,3\), then type \(3,2\). Receive \(4\), then type \(4,1\). Finally receive and type \(5\).

E: Receive all five letters, then type them from the top in the order \(5,4,3,2,1\).

Therefore the only impossible listed order is \(\boxed{4,5,2,3,1}\), choice D.
